title: An archaeological experiment on long bone breakage to extract marrow
author: Delphine Vettese
license_note: Confirmed via CrossRef DOI metadata: dx.doi.org/10.17504/protocols.io.be7fjhjn

steps.title: Set up work area and tools
steps.instruction: Extend the plastic sheet on the bench and place all required tools (hammer, anvil, plate, wooden sticks) within reach.

steps.title: Position recording camera
steps.instruction: Place the video camera so it records the entire test area for each bone breakage session.

steps.title: Prepare and code bone specimens
steps.instruction: Disarticulate each long bone, sort them by element (e.g., all humeri together), arrange them in a disordered pile, and assign a unique code combining the experimenter’s identifier and the bone number (e.g., 001-001 for the first bone of the first experimenter).

steps.title: Welcome participant and introduce experiment
steps.instruction: Greet the participant, explain the purpose of the experiment, and outline the overall procedure.

steps.title: Give instructions and objective
steps.instruction: State the objective: “To break the bones in order to extract the marrow so that it is suitable for consumption.” Explain that the participant may use any of the provided tools (hammer, anvil, plate, wooden sticks) or none, and that no additional procedure, demonstration, prescribed blow location, bone position, or scraping will be imposed.

steps.title: Suggest personal protective equipment
steps.instruction: Recommend that the participant wear gloves, safety goggles, and a lab coat before beginning.

steps.title: Encourage feedback and interaction
steps.instruction: Invite the participant to comment on his/her actions and interact with the observer throughout the session.

steps.title: Record experimenter code and hammerstone
steps.instruction: The observer writes the experimenter’s code on the data sheet and notes the identifier of the hammerstone (pebble) used for each bone.

steps.title: Photograph bones with scale (pre‑breakage)
steps.instruction: Take a clear photograph of each bone placed on a scale before any fracture occurs.

steps.title: Log basic bone characteristics
steps.instruction: On the experiment sheet record: bone element; lateralization (left/right); frozen or unfrozen status; degree of flesh removal (0 = with flesh, 1 = most of bone has flesh, 2 = most bone defleshed, 3 = fully defleshed).

steps.title: Start video recording and begin fracturing
steps.instruction: Turn on the camera and commence the bone‑breaking session.

substeps.instruction: Experimenter’s body position (sitting, standing, squatting, kneeling; specify both knees, left knee only, or right knee only).
Hand holding the hammerstone (right, left, both).
Bone position (on anvil, resting on ground, unsupported, percussion launched, other).
Angle of strike (perpendicular, left‑to‑right, right‑to‑left, arc of circle, toward the individual).
Location of blows (bone portion and side) as presence/absence.

steps.title: Conclude fracturing and stop recording
steps.instruction: When the participant decides the session is finished, turn off the camera.

steps.title: Photograph post‑breakage remains and marrow
steps.instruction: Photograph the bone fragments and the plate containing the extracted marrow, including a scale in the image.

steps.title: Weigh and dispose of marrow
steps.instruction: Weigh the collected marrow on a balance (tare the balance first), record the weight on the experiment sheet, then discard the marrow in an appropriate organic waste bin.

substeps.instruction: Quality of marrow (1 = not consumable, many splinters; 2 = mostly not consumable; 3 = half consumable; 4 = mostly consumable; 5 = fully consumable).
Perceived difficulty (1 = very easy, 2 = easy, 3 = moderate, 4 = difficult, 5 = very difficult).

steps.title: Collect bone fragments in coded bag
steps.instruction: Place all fragments of the current bone into a large bag labeled with the bone’s unique code and the participant’s identifier.

steps.title: Clean tools and replace PPE if needed
steps.instruction: If necessary, wipe the hammerstone and anvil; the participant may also clean his/her hands and replace gloves at any time, especially at the end of the session.

steps.title: Proceed to next bone element
steps.instruction: The participant selects the next bone specimen and repeats steps 7 through 18 until ten elements have been processed.
